item.title: Alibaba expects second-generation T-Head chip to tape out and enter production this year
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said on Aug. 20 that the company’s second-generation T-Head chip is expected to begin tape-out and production in the second half of this year. Alibaba said the chip will offer stronger computing performance and interconnect bandwidth, and that the company believes it can support large-model training workloads. An Alibaba Cloud supernode […]
item.content:encoded:
Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said on Aug. 20 that the company’s second-generation T-Head chip is expected to begin tape-out and production in the second half of this year. Alibaba said the chip will offer stronger computing performance and interconnect bandwidth, and that the company believes it can support large-model training workloads.

An Alibaba Cloud supernode built around the Zhenwu M890 chip has already entered scaled sales. Alibaba also said its T-Head unit has developed a full-stack chip portfolio covering GPUs, CPUs and networking chips, while the Zhenwu product line had served more than 650 customers by early August. [[IT Home, in Chinese]

The model supports native 4K image output and is designed to handle constraints involving subjects, counts, spatial relationships, text, layouts and visual styles. The company says the lightweight model improves identity preservation and […]
item.content:encoded:
SenseTime has open-sourced SenseNova U1.5 Lite, an 8-billion-parameter multimodal model designed to combine visual understanding, image generation and editing in one system. The model supports native 4K image output and is designed to handle constraints involving subjects, counts, spatial relationships, text, layouts and visual styles.

The company says the lightweight model improves identity preservation and spatial structure during editing, while adding controls such as bounding boxes, visual markers and multiple reference images. SenseNova U1.5 Lite is available through GitHub, Hugging Face and ModelScope. [[IT Home, in Chinese]

The two models made their global debut at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show on Aug. 21. The lineup includes both single- and dual-motor versions. The cars can […]
item.content:encoded:
BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao brand opened pre-orders for its first sedan lineup on Aug. 20, with the Formula S and Formula S GT priced from RMB230,000 to RMB280,000. The two models made their global debut at the 2026 Chengdu Auto Show on Aug. 21.

The lineup includes both single- and dual-motor versions. The cars can use a single motor rated at up to 300 kilowatts or a dual-motor setup rated at 190 kW and 300 kW, with a top speed of 240 kilometers per hour. The models are scheduled to launch in the third quarter. [[CnEVPost]

The device has a 6.39-inch OLED display with 2,232-by-1,320 resolution and a 96.1% screen-to-body ratio, with four 1.05-millimeter bezels. The phone is 6.68 millimeters […]
item.content:encoded:
At an Aug. 20 launch event, Huawei unveiled the Pura X View, a conventional smartphone with a wider 16:9.5 display instead of the tall screen format used by most slab phones. The device has a 6.39-inch OLED display with 2,232-by-1,320 resolution and a 96.1% screen-to-body ratio, with four 1.05-millimeter bezels.

The phone is 6.68 millimeters thick, weighs 201 grams and packs a 7,000mAh battery. Huawei opened reservations on Aug. 20, with in-store experiences scheduled to begin on Aug. 28. The design brings the wider viewing format associated with Huawei’s Pura X foldable line to a non-folding device. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: Alibaba’s AI spending lifts capex 75% as quarterly profit falls 76%
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Alibaba reported RMB268.95 billion in revenue for the quarter ended June 30, up 9% year on year, while net income attributable to ordinary shareholders fell 76% to RMB10.54 billion. Capital expenditure rose 75% to RMB67.68 billion, mainly as the company increased investment in AI infrastructure. Alibaba’s June-quarter results also showed operating cash flow of RMB22.95 […]
item.content:encoded:
Alibaba reported RMB268.95 billion in revenue for the quarter ended June 30, up 9% year on year, while net income attributable to ordinary shareholders fell 76% to RMB10.54 billion. Capital expenditure rose 75% to RMB67.68 billion, mainly as the company increased investment in AI infrastructure. Alibaba’s June-quarter results also showed operating cash flow of RMB22.95 billion.

Revenue from Alibaba’s AI cloud and computing services reached RMB48.44 billion, up 45%. AI-related product revenue reached RMB12.38 billion and continued to grow at a triple-digit rate for the 12th consecutive quarter. The company also reorganized its e-commerce, cloud-computing and AI-model businesses into new operating groups. [TechNode reporting]

item.title: China has more than 70 operational embodied-AI training grounds, report says
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: More than 70 embodied-AI training grounds had been built and put into operation across China by the end of June, according to a 2026 report from the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. Another 46 facilities were under construction or in the planning stage, with the sites spread across more than half of China’s […]
item.content:encoded:
More than 70 embodied-AI training grounds had been built and put into operation across China by the end of June, according to a 2026 report from the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. Another 46 facilities were under construction or in the planning stage, with the sites spread across more than half of China’s provincial-level regions.

The facilities provide physical environments for collecting real-world data, training models and testing robotic systems. Industrial manufacturing is the most common application, appearing in 86% of the training grounds, while the Yangtze River Delta, Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Pearl River Delta regions have emerged as the main clusters. [[IT Home, in Chinese]

item.title: Tech Odyssey Series: How a €30-a-month desk in Braga helped a startup reach 70 countries
item.dc:creator: TechNode Staff
item.description: In the previous episode of Tech Odyssey, we visited Coimbra to see how university research, applied R&D, and entrepreneurship come together in a small Portuguese city. This time, we head north to Braga, where Startup Braga is helping founders build companies for global markets from an affordable starting point. A workstation at Startup Braga costs […]
item.content:encoded:
In the previous episode of Tech Odyssey, we visited Coimbra to see how university research, applied R&D, and entrepreneurship come together in a small Portuguese city. This time, we head north to Braga, where Startup Braga is helping founders build companies for global markets from an affordable starting point.

A workstation at Startup Braga costs just €30 a month. ChemiTek, one of the companies that started there, now sells its solar-panel protection products in 70 countries, with local inventory in 50 of them.

Braga is not usually the first Portuguese city associated with startups. But inside Startup Braga, the city’s ambition is clear: companies may begin locally, but they are expected to think internationally from the start.

Startup Braga is based in GNRATION, a former building used by a national police force. After its rehabilitation project won Portugal’s National Rehabilitation Prize in 2014, the building was transformed into a public space for culture, technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship.

The incubator is part of InvestBraga, a municipal agency established in 2014 to promote innovation, entrepreneurship, investment, and economic development. It has since built a community of around 300 startups across software, AI, health technology, medical devices, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and nanotechnology. Around 20 startups are currently incubated on site.

Startup Braga runs programs for different stages, from ideation and pre-acceleration to incubation and open innovation. It also works closely with the University of Minho, the Clinical Academic Center of Braga, and the International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory.

One example is the Global Health Accelerator, developed with 2CA-Braga and INL. More than 40% of Portugal’s clinical trials are carried out at 2CA-Braga, giving health-focused startups access to a strong local research and clinical network.

ChemiTek is perhaps the clearest example of Braga’s global outlook.

Founded by César Martins in 2018, the company develops cleaning products, anti-static coatings, and hydrophobic coatings for solar panels. It started at Startup Braga, while the SBS Fund and other Portuguese partners joined its seed round in 2019.

Martins said Braga offered proximity, energy, and access to universities and research centers. But he also understands that Portugal’s domestic market is too small for most startups to stay local.

“Portugal is a small country,” he said. “You have to think about the global market from the beginning.”

Other companies at Startup Braga are taking different routes from research to market.

eDynamics is developing a digital health system that uses sensors and a smart insole to assess physical fatigue and predict injury risk. Its potential users include athletes and workers in physically demanding sectors such as logistics and retail.

The company was founded by three researchers whose work in rehabilitation robotics and wearable technology began at the University of Minho. After facing delays with manufacturing partners in India and China, the team decided to work with manufacturers closer to home in Portugal.

IPLEXMED is working on a more research-intensive challenge. The company is developing a graphene-based diagnostic device that could reduce the time needed to identify bacteria responsible for respiratory infections from more than seven hours to around 20 minutes.

It is still at the prototype and preclinical validation stage, with plans to enter the market in 2027. Like eDynamics, IPLEXMED began with university research before becoming a startup.

Startup Braga receives around 200 applications a year from international startups and works with Portugal’s Startup Visa program to support technology companies looking to establish or expand in the country.

For founders looking toward Asia, Macau and Hong Kong may offer potential entry points into the Chinese market. China’s manufacturing base and the application potential of AI, drones, and robotics are also attracting interest from Portuguese startups.

Braga is not trying to become another Lisbon or Porto. Its model is more focused: connect research institutions, incubators, and founders, then give companies enough support to take their first steps.

The €30 desk is only the starting point. The ambition, from the beginning, is global.

item.title: Why Unitree became the first humanoid robot company to go public in China
item.dc:creator: Jessie Wu
item.description: On Wednesday, Unitree Robotics debuted on the STAR Market of the Shanghai Stock Exchange under the ticker 688836.SH. On the same day, the 2026 World Robot Conference opened in Beijing. The timing was symbolic: humanoid robots are moving beyond labs and exhibitions and into the next stage of capital markets and commercial competition. Unitree priced […]
item.content:encoded:
On Wednesday, Unitree Robotics debuted on the STAR Market of the Shanghai Stock Exchange under the ticker 688836.SH. On the same day, the 2026 World Robot Conference opened in Beijing. The timing was symbolic: humanoid robots are moving beyond labs and exhibitions and into the next stage of capital markets and commercial competition.

Unitree priced its initial public offering on the STAR Market at RMB 150.80 ($22.41) per share, issuing 40,446,434 new A-shares and raising total proceeds of around RMB 6.099 billion ($910 million).

But Unitree was not a company that bet on humanoid robots from the beginning.

In 2016, founder Wang Xingxing left a university laboratory to start the company. At the time, China’s quadruped robot market was still at a very early stage. Compared with humanoid robots, quadruped robots were relatively easier to develop and commercialize in terms of mechanical design, motion control, and practical applications. Unitree chose to start with quadruped robots, launching the Go, A, and B series and gradually expanding into research, education, and industrial inspection.

This experience gave Unitree an early product and revenue base. From 2022 to 2025, revenue from its quadruped robot business grew from RMB 92.82 million ($13.79 million) to RMB 698 million ($103.72 million). Before humanoid robots became a major industry trend, Unitree had already built a foundation for commercial growth.

What truly changed Unitree’s growth trajectory was humanoid robots.

In 2023, revenue from Unitree’s humanoid robot business was only RMB 2.96 million ($440,000), accounting for less than 2% of its total revenue. By 2025, that figure had surged to RMB 868 million ($128.98 million), which made up more than 51% of the company’s total revenue. Humanoid robots had officially become the company’s main growth driver.

Products such as the H1 and G1 also helped Unitree move from being a robot demonstrator to becoming a robotics product company. In the past, a robot that could walk or run was already enough to become a highlight at an exhibition. But as the industry moves toward commercialization, the more important questions are whether robots can be produced reliably, sold consistently, and generate sustainable revenue.

Unitree has moved relatively quickly on this front.

In 2025, the company generated RMB 1.699 billion ($250 million) in revenue and RMB 278 million ($41.31 million) in net profit attributable to shareholders. At a time when many humanoid robot companies are still operating at a loss, Unitree has demonstrated a certain level of commercial viability. That has become an important foundation for its entry into the capital markets.

At the same time, Unitree’s IPO has arrived at an important moment for the industry.

In 2026, the humanoid robotics industry is increasingly shifting its focus from whether robots can be built to whether they can be put to practical use. Automakers, robotics companies, and AI firms are all pushing toward mass production and real-world deployment. The market is now paying closer attention to product capabilities, cost control, and the ability to scale production and delivery.

The listing of a robotics company with actual products, revenue, and profitability provides a concrete reference point for investors trying to understand the rapidly developing industry.

But going public does not mean Unitree has already won the next round of competition. For Unitree, the biggest challenge ahead may not be selling more robots, but making them smarter.

Over the past decade, Unitree’s strengths have largely been concentrated in mechanical design, motors, motion control, and robot hardware. But as humanoid robots enter commercial deployment, hardware alone may not be enough to create a long-term competitive advantage.

Robots ultimately need to understand the real world, make decisions based on their surroundings, and perform tasks that were not explicitly programmed in advance. The competition is therefore moving beyond the robot’s body and increasingly toward its brain.

Following its IPO, Unitree is also expected to increase investment in areas such as embodied AI foundation models. For a company that started in a university laboratory, going public marks the completion of one stage rather than the end of the journey.

Over the past decade, Unitree has shown that it can build robots, sell them, and generate meaningful revenue at scale. The next question is more straightforward: Can it turn its hardware advantage into AI capabilities and remain competitive in the next stage of embodied AI?

That may ultimately be more important than simply becoming the first humanoid robot company to go public on China’s A-share market.

item.title: Chery’s AiMOGA Robotics begins IPO preparations as it targets overseas markets
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Chery’s AiMOGA Robotics has started preparing for a potential standalone IPO and is in discussions over possible listing venues. The company has not announced a timetable or selected an exchange. Its leadership said a listing could provide funding for technology investment and overseas expansion. Incubated by Chery in January 2025, AiMOGA says it has delivered […]
item.content:encoded:
Chery’s AiMOGA Robotics has started preparing for a potential standalone IPO and is in discussions over possible listing venues. The company has not announced a timetable or selected an exchange. Its leadership said a listing could provide funding for technology investment and overseas expansion.

Incubated by Chery in January 2025, AiMOGA says it has delivered more than 3,000 robots globally, including 2,000 overseas, with operations in more than 60 countries and regions. The company is targeting 10,000 global deliveries next year and has deployed 110 humanoid police robots in several Chinese cities. [[Reuters]

item.title: Unitree launches a seven-axis dexterous arm starting at RMB9,900
item.dc:creator: TechNode Feed
item.description: Unitree has launched a bionic seven-axis dexterous arm starting at RMB9,900. The company’s R1 arm has a claimed repeat-positioning accuracy of about 0.1 millimeter, maximum joint speeds of more than 180 degrees per second, a maximum reach of 650 millimeters with a dexterous hand, and a rated payload of 2 kilograms. The 5.5-kilogram arm includes […]
item.content:encoded:
Unitree has launched a bionic seven-axis dexterous arm starting at RMB9,900. The company’s R1 arm has a claimed repeat-positioning accuracy of about 0.1 millimeter, maximum joint speeds of more than 180 degrees per second, a maximum reach of 650 millimeters with a dexterous hand, and a rated payload of 2 kilograms.

The 5.5-kilogram arm includes force feedback and collision detection, runs on an Ubuntu-based development environment, and supports XT30 and CAN485 interfaces. Unitree said it plans to open-source the arm’s control software and interfaces, with target applications including research, education, industrial assembly and service robots. [[IT Home, in Chinese]
